provenance.note: Arithmetic components are derived from the price panel. Judgment components were supplied 2026-08-26 with sourced reasoning. MID-CYCLE MANUAL RUN: judgment written 2026-08-26, five calendar days after the 2026-08-21 close this file reads. Two of the five sessions in the week window (Mon 08-24, Tue 08-25) had already traded. The three catalysts that dominate the window -- July core PCE and NVDA earnings (both 08-26), and the Warsh Jackson Hole keynote (08-28) -- were all still ahead, and the pinned research snapshot (2026-08-24) carries no post-08-21 outcomes. The week horizon is still not a clean ex-ante forecast and must not be graded as one.

day.unavailable: The day horizon needs daily bars; the upstream feed commits Friday closes only.

why: Archetype 1 has Industrials at +29.4 pct absolute, -1.9 pts excess -- essentially in line with SPY, neither a leader nor a laggard in a steady mid-cycle expansion (The Full Regime-Sector Matrix).

The growth signal underneath is genuinely strong: Empire State manufacturing hit 20.6, a four-year high, with new orders 17.3, and composite PMI backlogs are at 2022 highs (wiki/economic-calendar.md@63b4d3ba).
risks: The panel ranks Industrials 11th of 11 on the week at -2.56 pts vs SPY and -4.08 on the month, which contradicts the in-line archetype prior. Manufacturing PMI at 53.2 is a 5-month low even as services hit 56.8, and Schwab places Industrials among underperformers in the 12 months after a first hike (panel metrics, this file; wiki/economic-calendar.md@63b4d3ba; Sector Macro Sensitivity Matrix).

why: Breadth is the weakest of the eleven on the week (20.0) and only 40.0 on the month, so the sector is being carried by few names -- the arithmetic is the binding evidence here, not the archetype prior (panel metrics, this file).

SSGA classifies Industrials only a Tier 2 positive responder to the 10Y (R2 0.05, below the 0.08 strong threshold), so the rate backdrop is close to neutral for the sector either way (Sector Macro Sensitivity Matrix).
risks: Durable goods orders on 08-26 are the swing print: deeply negative would show capex caution spreading beyond housing (wiki/economic-calendar.md@63b4d3ba).

extracts.lead_summary: Industrials are the pulse of the economy. When the factories hum, the market sings. When they go silent, everything else follows.
